choices.text: Hydrochlorothiazide, to lower urinary calcium excretion

choices.label: B
choices.text: Furosemide, to increase tubular flow through the medulla

choices.label: C
choices.text: Acetazolamide, to alkalinize the urine in the proximal tubule

choices.label: D
choices.text: Spironolactone, to block aldosterone in the collecting duct

choices.label: E
choices.text: Allopurinol, to reduce hepatic production of uric acid

explanation.summary: Thiazide diuretics are used in MSK stone prevention because they lower urinary calcium excretion.
explanation.whyCorrect: For prevention of recurrent kidney stones in MSK, therapy consists of lifestyle changes, drug therapy, or both, with specific recommendations based on 24-hour urine collection results. The drug therapy the lecture cites is a thiazide diuretic, which lowers urinary calcium excretion and thereby reduces calcium stone formation.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Loop diuretics are not the cited preventive therapy and do not lower urinary calcium the way thiazides do.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Acetazolamide is not part of MSK stone prevention in this lecture, and MSK patients already risk acidosis from distal tubular dysfunction.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Aldosterone blockade does not address urinary calcium excretion, the target of preventive drug therapy in MSK.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The stones of MSK are calcium stones, so reducing uric acid production does not address their formation.

questions.topicName: Medullary Sponge Kidney

questions.stem: A 31-year-old man newly diagnosed with medullary sponge kidney asks whether he will eventually need dialysis. Which of the following is the most accurate response regarding his long-term kidney function?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Function usually stays normal unless stones or infections recur repeatedly

choices.label: B
choices.text: Function declines steadily to kidney failure in most patients by middle age

choices.label: C
choices.text: Function is preserved only if the medullary cysts are drained early

choices.label: D
choices.text: Function is lost rapidly once the cysts extend into the renal cortex

choices.label: E
choices.text: Function depends chiefly on starting a thiazide at the time of diagnosis

explanation.summary: Kidney function in MSK remains normal in most patients; ESRD is rare and tied to recurrent obstruction or infection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Kidney function tends to remain normal in most patients with MSK unless they have repeated obstruction with stones or repeated infections. Only rarely, in patients with recurrent obstruction or infections, does end-stage renal disease develop. The overall prognosis is excellent.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Steady progression to renal failure is not the natural history; MSK is a benign disorder that usually spares kidney function.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cyst drainage is not part of MSK management and is not what preserves renal function.
whyWrongByChoice.D: MSK does not involve the cortex; the disease is confined to the medulla.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thiazides help prevent recurrent stones but the disease's excellent prognosis does not hinge on starting one at diagnosis.

questions.topicName: Medullary Sponge Kidney

questions.stem: Several members of a family have medullary sponge kidney, and investigators studying such families have proposed a candidate gene. A mutation in the gene encoding which of the following proteins has been suggested, though not proven, to cause this disorder?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factor

choices.label: B
choices.text: Polycystin-1 transmembrane protein

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fibrillin-1 extracellular matrix protein

choices.label: D
choices.text: Type IV collagen alpha-5 chain

choices.label: E
choices.text: Aquaporin-2 collecting-duct water channel

explanation.summary: A GDNF mutation has been proposed as a cause of MSK, but no definitive genetic cause has been identified.
explanation.whyCorrect: MSK can cluster in families, suggesting inheritable components, and some researchers have suggested that the cause might be a mutation in the gene for glial cell-derived neurotrophic factor (GDNF). However, a definitive genetic cause has not been identified, and the exact genetic basis remains unknown.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Polycystin mutations underlie polycystic kidney disease, not the proposed genetics of MSK.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fibrillin-1 mutations cause Marfan syndrome, an occasional MSK association, but fibrillin is not the candidate gene proposed for MSK itself.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Type IV collagen defects cause hereditary glomerular basement membrane disease, not a collecting-duct malformation like MSK.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Aquaporin-2 relates to renal water handling; it is not the gene suggested in familial MSK.
